text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The DOS PC platform began with the release of the IBM Personal Computer in 1981 and became one of the most important gaming platforms of the 1980s and 1990s. Early DOS games were built around text displays, CGA and EGA graphics, and simple PC speaker audio before expanding with VGA graphics, sound cards, and CD-ROM support. The platform hosted many influential genres including adventure games, role-playing games, simulations, strategy games, and early first-person shooters. Titles from this era helped establish PC gaming traditions that continue today, including modding, shareware distribution, and keyboard-based controls.
